options.text: Package units have 12–15 EER, equivalent to split systems; rooftop location improves cooling efficiency due to better air circulation.
Package units achieve 6–8 EER only because the condenser is exposed to typhoons; no inherent efficiency disadvantage vs. split systems.

rationale.a: Package units have 12–15 EER, equivalent to split systems; rooftop location improves cooling efficiency due to better air circulation.
rationale.c: Package units achieve 6–8 EER only because the condenser is exposed to typhoons; no inherent efficiency disadvantage vs. split systems.
rationale.d: Package units are actually more efficient than split systems (14+ EER) because single-unit design eliminates refrigerant line losses; part-load efficiency is identical to split type.
rationale.correct: Typical package unit EER is 9–12 EER (MEPS 8.6 minimum, market average >10) (COP 2.8–3.2, source: Energy Efficiency Labeling Scheme). Package units operate at fixed capacity with on/off cycling, lacking modulation capability; at part-load conditions (e.g., 50% load), the compressor cycles on/off rather than throttling efficiently like VRF systems (which can vary capacity continuously). This on/off cycling wastes energy during off periods and reduces overall seasonal efficiency. Source: ALE-UTIL-002-04 Package Units section.
rationale.takeaway: Package (rooftop) units trade efficiency for simplicity; EER 8–11 is acceptable for small buildings with predictable loads but unsuitable for tropical climate where part-load operation dominates.
